summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that Plato and Nietzsche use stylistic masks (dialogue and aphorism) to overcome the limitations of written philosophy. These masks communicate experiential states rather than doctrines, forcing readers into active interpretation. Misreadings are inevitable and serve a pedagogical function, exposing the reader's own inadequacies. The success of this strategy is measured not by absence of misreading but by its ability to provoke genuine philosophical activity.
